# Roleplay Rule 7 - Death Amnesia / NLR
Your character is not allowed to remember the person who killed them; they may [bold]not[/bold] describe the person who killed them at all. Keep the identity of the killer anonymous; it’s more fun for others that way. This may be referred to in-character as “death amnesia,” but frequently out-of-character you’ll hear this as the “new-life rule” (NLR).
Death occurs only once your health indicator reads “Dead,” you may exit your character’s body as a ghost, and you can access the “Dead” chat as a ghost. Being in “Crit” does not count as dying, but [italic]your character should only vaguely know what happens while they are in crit,[/italic] as if they were fading in and out of consciousness.
Additionally, sleeping should be treated as you’d expect: your character shouldn’t know what happens while they’re asleep. (Otherwise, they’d still be awake.)
Your character is allowed to remember what injury might've killed them, such as a gunshot, being stabbed, or where they died. Otherwise, as a rule of thumb, your character shouldn’t remember the events leading up to their death, such as the last 5 minutes before they died.
## Precedents
Acceptable: - Saying you got killed by a stab wound in maintenance, even though you died to an armblade. - Reporting to [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] that you died in [color=#c8a404][bold]Engineering[/bold][/color] to a gunshot wound.
Prohibited: - Explaining that a Vox male stabbed you. - Explaining that a [textlink="Heretic" link="Heretics"] killed you. - Explaining a moth with blue wings and green eyes killed you. - Saying you got killed by an armblade. - Saying you got killed with a Bulldog shotgun.
